references.text: Here the question is raised about who believes the message, which mirrors Jesus' question to the Jews as to why they do not believe him when he speaks the truth.
Jeremiah is sent to speak the truth to a people who refuse to listen and believe, a situation that reflects the opposition Jesus meets in John 8:45.
Jesus explains directly that they do not believe in him because they are not of his sheep, and that they do not believe due to their unwillingness toward the truth he speaks.
John comments that even though Jesus had performed so many signs, they did not believe in him, and refers to Isaiah saying that God has blinded their eyes so that they cannot see the truth.
